title: Late Payments Are Quietly Killing Your Contractor Relationships
summary: I lost a designer I really liked working with. Not because the work dried up or because she found a better gig. She left because I paid her 11 days late.
body_text: I lost a designer I really liked working with. Not because the work dried up or because she found a better gig. She left because I paid her 11 days late. Twice. She never said anything the first time. The second time, she sent a polite email saying she was "reprioritizing her client list" and wished me well. I found out later from a mutual contact that she had a rule: two late payments and she moves on. No drama, no second chances. She just quietly stops taking your calls. That stung. But the more I talked to other founders about it, the more I realized this is happening everywhere. Good contractors leave. They don't tell you why. And the ones who replace them are never quite as good. Contractors remember everything about how you pay Full-time employees have a cushion. They get paid on a schedule, automatically, from a system that doesn't forget. If payroll is a day late because of a bank holiday, it's annoying but not existential. Contractors don't have that cushion. Many of them are managing cash flow across multiple clients. A late payment from you might mean they can't pay their own bills on time. It might mean they have to dip into savings or delay paying a subcontractor. The stress of chasing invoices is real and it's exhausting. So they develop systems. Internal rules. Some will send one follow-up and then wait. Others have the two-strike rule like my designer. The best contractors, the ones you actually want to keep, have enough demand that they don't need to tolerate late payers. They just move on to clients who pay on time. You'll never hear about this directly. Nobody sends an email saying "you pay too slowly, I'm leaving." They just get busy. They start taking longer to respond. Eventually they're gone and you're back on Upwork. The reputation damage happens behind your back Contractors talk to each other. Especially within niches. The freelance designers in your city know each other. The data labellers working on AI projects compare notes. The UGC creators in your vertical have group chats. When someone asks "hey, have you worked with [your company]?", the answer includes how you pay. Not just how much. How reliably. A company that pays $50/hour but takes 45 days will lose to a company that pays $40/hour and pays within a week. I've seen this happen. We experienced this firsthand when we were running UGC campaigns for Pray Screen. We were managing 30+ creators and payments were a mess. Spreadsheets, different payment methods, manual bank transfers. Some creators got paid fast, some waited weeks depending on when we got around to processing their batch. The ones who waited started declining new campaigns. We didn't connect the dots until we noticed the same creators kept saying no. Late payments actually cost more This is counterintuitive. You'd think delaying payment saves money in the short term, or at least preserves cash flow. But the math doesn't work out. When a good contractor leaves, you spend time finding a replacement. That search takes hours. Then the new person needs to ramp up, learn your codebase or brand guidelines, figure out your communication style. That ramp period is expensive because you're paying for slower, lower-quality output while they get up to speed. I ran the numbers once after losing a developer. The contractor was billing $6,000/month. He left because I was consistently 2-3 weeks late paying invoices. Finding his replacement took three weeks. The new person took another month to match his output. Between the search time, onboarding, and reduced productivity, I estimated the transition cost about $12,000. If I had just paid the original guy on time, I'd have saved that entirely. There's also the quality issue. Top-tier contractors can afford to be selective. If you develop a reputation for slow payments, you're fishing from a smaller pool. The people willing to work with a known late payer are often the ones who don't have better options. That's a selection effect you don't want. The compounding problem Late payments rarely happen in isolation. If you're paying one contractor late, you're probably paying several late. The reason is usually systemic: you don't have a payment process, or the person responsible for payments is also doing twelve other things, or you're waiting for invoices to pile up before processing them in a batch. Each late payment is a small crack. One late payment, the contractor shrugs it off. Two, they start looking around. Three, they've already mentally moved on. By the time you notice the pattern, you've burned through goodwill with multiple people at once. I've talked to founders who lost three or four contractors in the same quarter and couldn't figure out why. When I asked about their payment timeline, it was always the same story. "We usually pay within 30 days. Sometimes it takes a bit longer." That "bit longer" was killing them. What "on time" actually means Net-30 is standard in a lot of industries. It's also too slow for most contractors. Especially smaller ones. Especially international ones who might be dealing with additional transfer delays on top of your payment terms. In my experience, here's how contractors actually feel about payment timing: Within 7 days of invoice: you're a great client. They'll prioritize your work, respond faster, and go above and beyond. This is rare enough that it stands out. Within 14 days: totally acceptable. Most contractors are fine with this and consider it normal. Within 30 days: tolerated but not loved. If everything else about working with you is great, they'll stay. But you have no margin for error. One late payment on top of net-30 and you're at 45+ days. That's when people start leaving. Beyond 30 days: you're losing people. They just might not tell you yet. The excuse that doesn't work "We're a startup, cash flow is tight." I've said this myself. It feels like a valid reason. But your contractor doesn't care about your runway. They did the work. They sent the invoice. They held up their end. If you genuinely can't afford to pay contractors on time, you have a business problem that late payments won't solve. You're just transferring your cash flow problem to someone with less financial cushion than you. And if you can afford to pay on time but just don't have a system for it, that's worse. That means the only thing standing between you and retaining great contractors is a process you haven't bothered to build. Building a payment system that doesn't fail The fix isn't complicated. It's just not the kind of thing most founders prioritize until they've already lost someone. Set a payment day. Pick a day of the week or month. Every invoice received before that day gets paid on that day. No exceptions, no "I'll get to it later." Put it on your calendar if you have to. Remove yourself from the loop if you're the bottleneck. If payments wait because you're busy, delegate. Give someone else the ability to approve and send payments. Or better yet, use a system where payment happens with one action instead of a chain of manual steps. This is a big part of why we built Grade. When we were managing 30+ creators for Pray Screen, the payment bottleneck was always us. We'd batch invoices, forget about them, then scramble to pay everyone at once. Some people waited weeks. Now with Grade, you add contractors with their email, they pick their payment method, and you pay everyone with one click. The whole point is to make it so easy that there's no reason to delay. Send confirmation when you pay. A quick "payment sent" message goes a long way. Contractors shouldn't have to guess whether their invoice was received or when money is coming. If you use a platform that sends automatic notifications, even better. The contractors you keep are the ones you pay I think about that designer sometimes. She was good. She understood our brand, worked fast, and didn't need hand-holding. I lost her over 11 days. Not a rate dispute, not a creative disagreement. Just 11 days. The best retention strategy for contractors isn't higher rates or better perks. It's paying them the amount you agreed on, when you agreed to pay it. That's the bar. It's not high. But a surprising number of companies can't clear it. Pay your contractors on time. Every time. The ones worth keeping will notice.

title: Compass Announces Inducement Grants Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
summary: BOSTON, Jan. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Compass Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: CMPX), a clinical-stage, oncology-focused biopharmaceutical company developing proprietary antibody-based therapeutics to treat multiple human diseases, today announced it granted stock options to two new employees under
body_text: PDF Version BOSTON, Jan. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Compass Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: CMPX), a clinical-stage, oncology-focused biopharmaceutical company developing proprietary antibody-based therapeutics to treat multiple human diseases, today announced it granted stock options to two new employees under the Company’s 2025 Inducement Plan and as a material inducement to their employment in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). The Company granted non-qualified stock options to purchase 1,000,000 shares of common stock to its newly appointed Chief Commercial Officer, Arjun Prasad, and also granted non-qualified stock options to purchase 1,000,000 shares of common stock to its newly appointed Chief Medical Officer, Cynthia Sirard. The stock options have an exercise price of $5.17 per share, which is equal to the closing price of the Company’s common stock on January 2, 2026. The options have a 10-year term and vest over four years, with 25% of the shares vesting on the one-year anniversary of the grant date and the remaining 75% vesting in 36 substantially equal monthly installments thereafter, subject to each respective employee’s continued service with the Company. These inducement grants were approved by Compass Therapeutics Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors as a material inducement to employment. They were granted outside of the Company’s 2020 Stock Option and Incentive Plan and are subject to the Company’s 2025 Inducement Plan and the applicable award agreements. About Compass Therapeutics Compass Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage oncology-focused biopharmaceutical company developing proprietary antibody-based therapeutics to treat multiple human diseases. Compass’s scientific focus is on the relationship between angiogenesis, the immune system, and tumor growth. The company pipeline of novel product candidates is designed to target multiple critical biological pathways required for an effective anti-tumor response. These include modulation of the microvasculature via angiogenesis-targeted agents, induction of a potent immune response via activators on effector cells in the tumor microenvironment, and alleviation of immunosuppressive mechanisms used by tumors to evade immune surveillance. Compass plans to advance its product candidates through clinical development and commercialization as both standalone therapies and in combination with proprietary pipeline antibodies based on supportive clinical and nonclinical data. The company was founded in 2014 and is headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. For more information, visit the Compass Therapeutics website at https://www.compasstherapeutics.com . title: Elevating Performance: How H.B. Fuller Powers the Future of Elevator Manufacturing
summary: Discover how H.B. Fuller is transforming elevator manufacturing with advanced adhesive technologies—supporting smart elevators, glass designs, and high-performance bonding solutions for doors, panels, electronics, and more.
body_text: In the fast-moving world of elevator manufacturing, choosing the right elevator adhesives and bonding solutions is critical to ensure safety, durability, and innovation. H.B. Fuller, a global leader in innovative industrial adhesives, brings a specialized portfolio tailored for the vertical transportation industry—with products that support structural integrity, modern design, and next-generation electronics in elevators. What is the latest in interior elevator trends? 1. Minimalist and Seamless Design Hidden lighting, flush-mounted controls , and smooth, clean lines Matte metal finishes like brushed brass, gunmetal, and black stainless steel Frameless glass walls and low-profile button panels 2. Panoramic Glass Cabins Full 360° glass elevators with minimal structural framing Use of UV- and sound-resistant adhesives for seamless bonding 3. Custom Art and Digital Walls Backlit LED panels with changing scenery, brand visuals, or ambient effects Use of printed glass or digital canvases for immersive experiences Adhesives needed to securely mount delicate electronics and panels 4. Sustainable & Natural Materials Wood veneers, stone panels, bamboo, and leather accents Use of VOC-free adhesives and eco-certified bonding systems Focus on recyclable and low-emission components 5. Ultra-Quiet & Smooth Interiors Acoustic paneling and vibration-damping materials Noise-reducing adhesives and construction to boost ride quality Perfect for residential towers, executive offices, and boutique hotels 6. Touchless and Smart Controls Integration of touchless call systems, mobile app controls, and AI-enhanced displays Requires microelectronic adhesives for screen bonding, sensor attachment, and protection against tampering or wear Fire Resistance: A Critical Factor in Elevator Safety In vertical transportation systems, fire resistance isn't optional—it's essential. Elevators run through every floor of a building, often acting as a vertical conduit for heat and smoke in the event of a fire. That's why using fire-rated materials, especially for door panels, car cladding, and insulation, is vital to meet building codes and protect passenger safety. H.B. Fuller offers adhesives that comply with UNI EN 45545-2 fire safety standards (R1 HL 1-3) . These products provide high mechanical strength and elasticity while withstanding extreme temperatures—ensuring that structural bonds hold when they’re needed most. Smart Elevators & AI Integration Elevators are becoming more intelligent with the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT). These technologies enable features like predictive maintenance, real-time traffic analysis, and personalized user experiences. Some systems even incorporate facial recognition to automatically identify users and direct them to their designated floors, enhancing convenience and efficiency. Elevator Decorations Made with Removeable Adhesives A rising trend in commercial and public spaces is the use of elevator wraps—vibrant, large-format graphics applied to elevator doors and interiors for advertising, branding, or decorative purposes. These wraps transform otherwise utilitarian surfaces into dynamic visual experiences, capturing attention in high-traffic areas like malls, hospitals, airports, and corporate offices. A key innovation enabling this trend is H.B. Fuller’s microsphere adhesive technology , which offers a unique solution for removable and repositionable graphics. This water-based acrylic technology allows graphics to be applied cleanly, repositioned multiple times, and removed without damage or adhesive residue—ideal for temporary campaigns or seasonal branding. As elevator wraps continue to gain popularity, H.B. Fuller’s microsphere technology is helping reshape how brands engage with audiences. Freight Elevators Freight elevators are experiencing a surge in innovation and demand, driven by the rapid expansion of e-commerce, warehouse automation, and the need for efficient vertical logistics. In 2025, the market is projected to grow significantly, with key trends including the integration of IoT-enabled systems for real-time performance monitoring, energy-efficient designs, and enhanced safety features . As warehouses become larger and more complex, freight elevators are increasingly being paired with automated storage and retrieval systems to streamline operations and reduce manual labor. Manufacturers are also focusing on customization to meet specific industrial requirements, offering high-capacity, durable solutions that can handle the rigorous demands of modern supply chains. These advancements position freight elevators as critical infrastructure in high-speed, data-driven logistics environments. Electrification of Elevators The electrification of elevators represents a transformative shift for industrial elevator manufacturers, offering new opportunities to enhance performance, sustainability, and integration with smart building systems. By replacing traditional hydraulic or mechanical systems with advanced electric drives and controls, manufacturers can deliver elevators that are more energy-efficient, quieter, and easier to maintain. Electrified systems also enable precise motion control, regenerative braking, and real-time diagnostics, which contribute to reduced operational costs and improved user experience. As demand grows for eco-friendly and connected infrastructure, embracing electrification positions manufacturers to meet evolving regulatory standards and customer expectations while driving innovation in vertical transportation solutions. H.B. Fuller’s suite of electric battery solutions —such as EV Bond structural adhesives, EV Protect flame-retardant encapsulants, and EV Seal moisture-resistant sealing systems—offers industrial elevator manufacturers a robust foundation for integrating high-performance battery modules into vertical transportation systems.

title: Park Dental Partners Expands Presence in Arizona with Addition of Ironwood Dental
summary: MINNEAPOLIS, Jan. 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Park Dental Partners, Inc. (NASDAQ: PARK) (the Company), a leading dental resource organization, announced that on January 23, 2026, Ironwood Dental, located in Tucson, Arizona, joins the Park Dental Partners network of affiliated dental practices.
body_text: Park Dental Partners Expands Presence in Arizona with Addition of Ironwood Dental January 28, 2026 PDF Version MINNEAPOLIS, Jan. 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Park Dental Partners, Inc. (NASDAQ: PARK) (the Company), a leading dental resource organization, announced that on January 23, 2026, Ironwood Dental, located in Tucson, Arizona, joins the Park Dental Partners network of affiliated dental practices. This is the Company’s second practice in the state and the first in Tucson. Terms of the transaction were not disclosed. “We are very pleased to add a second practice in Arizona that aligns with our organization’s philosophy of supporting dentists and dental practices that put patients first and provides high-quality, patient-centered care,” said Pete Swenson, Park Dental Partners Chief Executive Officer. “We are pleased to support their efforts moving forward. We are also excited to enter the Tucson market with our proven operating model and increase our presence in Arizona.” Entering Tucson Market with Ironwood Dental Ironwood Dental marks the Company’s second location in Arizona and first in the Tucson, Arizona market. The practice offers comprehensive general dentistry services and is led by Dr. Alyssa Holmes, a highly trained general dentist with a dual background in dentistry and public health. She earned her Doctor of Dental Medicine and Master of Public Health degrees from A.T. Still University, graduating with honors and receiving multiple leadership awards. She went on to complete a rigorous Advanced Education in General Dentistry (AEGD) residency through NYU Langone Hospital, gaining experience in complex restorative, surgical, and digital dentistry. Dr. Holmes excels in prosthodontics, implant restorations, oral surgery, and patient education. “Ironwood Dental is another great example of the type of high-quality, community-focused practice we are pleased to welcome into our organization,” said Dr. Chris Steele, Park Dental Partners Chief Clinical Officer, General Practices. “Dr. Holmes’ advanced dental training and master’s in public health have resulted in the Ironwood Dental practice being a true asset in the community. Her experience as an advanced clinician and perspective of oral and public health will be a great asset as we grow our presence in Arizona.” A Growing Network with a Community Mindset With this affiliation, Park Dental Partners continues to build a strong, mission‑driven network of dental practices rooted in quality, patient-centered care and clinical excellence. About PARK DENTAL PARTNERS Park Dental Partners, Inc., and its subsidiaries (NASDAQ:PARK) is a dental resource organization that has put patients first since establishment of its general dentistry group in 1972. The Company provides comprehensive business support services, including clinical team members, administrative personnel, facilities, and equipment, to its affiliated general and multi-specialty dental practices. The Company currently employs over 200 dentists across 88 practice locations in 3 states. The Company’s clinical support team consists of over 900 hygienists, dental assistants, and patient care coordinators that support affiliated dentists in operating their practices. Park Dental Partners is based in Roseville, Minnesota. For more information, please visit www.parkdentalpartners.com . body_text: View All News Driven Brands Announces Closing of Sale of International Car Wash Business January 27, 2026 CHARLOTTE, N.C.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Driven Brands Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: DRVN) (“Driven Brands” or the “Company”) today announced the completion of the sale of IMO, its international car wash business, to Franchise Equity Partners. “The completion of this transaction is a strategic milestone for Driven Brands, sharpening our focus on what we do best — scaling our industry-leading Take 5 business and driving consistent cash generation from our franchise brands,” said Danny Rivera, President and Chief Executive Officer. “I want to thank everyone involved for their hard work in closing the transaction. This divestiture simplifies our portfolio, strengthens our balance sheet, and further positions Driven Brands to generate value for shareholders.” Under the terms of the agreement, Franchise Equity Partners paid Driven Brands total aggregate consideration of approximately € 411 million. Cash proceeds from the transaction will primarily be used to pay down debt. The Company plans to report the results of the Car Wash segment as discontinued operations beginning in the fourth quarter of 2025. Auto Glass Now, currently reported in the Corporate & Other segment, will be reported as a stand-alone segment beginning in the fourth quarter of 2025. In addition, the Company expects to furnish a Form 8-K with the Securities and Exchange Commission in mid-February to provide unaudited historical recast quarterly financial operating results for the first three quarters of fiscal 2025, reflecting the Company’s updated segment reporting structure resulting from the completed disposition of its international car wash business. Advisors Rothschild & Co. served as financial advisor to Driven Brands. About Driven Brands Driven Brands™, headquartered in Charlotte, NC, is the largest automotive services company in North America, providing a range of consumer and commercial automotive services, including paint, collision, glass, vehicle repair, oil change and maintenance. Driven Brands is the parent company of some of North America’s leading automotive service businesses including Take 5 Oil Change®, Meineke Car Care Centers®, Maaco®, 1-800-Radiator & A/C®, Auto Glass Now®, and CARSTAR®. Driven Brands has approximately 4,200 locations across North America, and services tens of millions of vehicles annually. Driven Brands’ network generates approximately $1.8 billion in annual revenue from approximately $6.1 billion in system-wide sales. body_text: Life Science デジタルデザインはどのように抗ウイルス薬開発を変革しているのか BY 岡部 篤俊 , 落田 温子博士 & アバ・E・レフラー博士 Jan 29, 2026 新型コロナウイルス感染症（COVID-19）が世界的なパンデミックとして発生した際、世界は前例のないスピードでワクチンと治療薬の開発・供給に尽力しました。この目覚ましい成果は数百万もの命を救い、グローバルな科学協力の力を証明しました。しかし、SARS-CoV-2は進化を続けており、パンデミックを引き起こす可能性のある他のコロナウイルスも依然として懸念されています。次の感染拡大に備えるためには、既知のコロナウイルスおよび今後出現する可能性のあるコロナウイルス全般に効果を発揮する抗ウイルス薬を開発する必要があります。 武田薬品工業とSchrödinger社は最近、この目標達成に向けて重要な進展を遂げました。両社は共同で、コロナウイルスの主要プロテアーゼであるMproの強力な非共有結合阻害剤を発見しました。Mproは、コロナウイルスがヒト細胞内で複製するために不可欠な酵素です。この研究成果は「 Journal of Medicinal Chemistry 」誌に掲載され、両社のチームが構造に基づいた設計と予測モデリングを活用して、次世代抗ウイルス薬候補の迅速な発見を実現した方法が詳述されています。 Mpro：ウイルスの弱点 SARS、MERS、そしてSARS-CoV-2といったコロナウイルスは、増殖のためにMproという酵素に依存しており、この酵素を使って長いウイルス蛋白質を複製に必要な小さな断片に切断します。ヒトにはこれに相当する酵素が存在しないため、Mproはオフターゲット効果のリスクを最小限に抑えながらウイルスの複製を阻害できる抗ウイルス薬にとって、特に魅力的な標的となります。 既存の経口Mpro阻害剤は、COVID-19パンデミックにおける抗ウイルス治療薬への緊急ニーズに対応して開発されました。これらの薬剤は、ウイルス量を減少させ、重症化を防ぐことで、何百万人もの患者を救ってきました。現在、この分野では、薬物相互作用の可能性を低減し、より幅広いコロナウイルス株に対して活性を示すなど、プロファイルが改善された分子を開発することで、この基盤の上にさらに発展させる機会が生まれています。このような進歩は、ウイルスが進化し続ける中でも、将来の治療法が効果的であり続けることを保証するのに役立ちます。 新たなパンデミックの脅威に備えるため、シュレーディンガー社と武田薬品工業のチームは、強力で安全、かつ幅広いコロナウイルスに対して活性を示す次世代の非共有結合型Mpro阻害剤を設計するという明確な目標を設定しました。 統合型「予測優先」設計戦略 Mproは構造的に十分に解明されていますが、高い効力と幅広い効果を兼ね備えた阻害剤を設計するには、精密な分子設計が必要です。武田薬品は、医薬品化学と構造生物学における深い専門知識を有していました。両社のチームは協力し、物理ベースのFEP+（自由エネルギー摂動法）や、分子設計のためのクラウドネイティブな共同作業環境であるLiveDesignなど、Schrödinger社のソリューションスイートを活用しました。これらのツールにより、24時間体制で稼働する機敏な創薬エンジンを構築することができました。 まず、Schrödinger社のGlideソフトウェアを用いて、武田薬品が保有する150万種類の化合物ライブラリに対して大規模な仮想スクリーニングを実施しました。このアプローチにより、有望な候補化合物を迅速に数種類に絞り込むことができ、従来の手法で実験のみを行った場合数ヶ月かかる作業を、大幅に短縮することができました。 武田薬品の研究者たちは、初期のヒット分子の一つ（ピペラジン骨格、つまり多くの医薬品の基本的な化学骨格として用いられる2つの窒素原子を含む6員環構造を持つ化合物）が結合したSARS-CoV-2 MproのX線結晶構造を決定しました。この構造解析により、分子がMproの活性部位にどのように結合するかが明らかになり、さらなる最適化のための正確な指針が得られました。 この段階で、Schrödinger社のFEP+シミュレーションがイノベーションの原動力となりました。FEP+は、タンパク質の柔軟性や、Gln189、Met49、Met165といった重要なアミノ酸の誘導適合運動を考慮に入れ、結合親和性の変化を驚異的な精度で予測します。これらの微細な変化によって、新たな結合機会を生み出す隠れた「クリプティックポケット」が開きます。 私たちはLiveDesign内で直接FEP+計算を実行し、グローバルな学際的チームに、設計、予測、分析、共同作業のための統一されたインターフェースを提供しました。すべての実験データとインシリコ解析結果が一箇所に集約されていたため、私たちの作業は滞ることなく進みました。日本の武田薬品のチームメンバーが計算を終えると、ニューヨーク、ポートランド、サンディエゴのSchrödinger社のチームメンバーがすぐに次のステップに取りかかることができました。これにより、プロジェクトは24時間体制で進行しました。LiveDesignの統合モデリングツールとコラボレーションインターフェースは、データ、モデル、結果をリアルタイムで共有することで、部門間の壁を取り除くのにも役立ち、より迅速で創造的な設計サイクルと、シームレスな24時間体制の意思決定を実現しました。私たちは7,000種類以上の化合物を計算によって評価し、実際に合成したのはわずか85種類でした。これは、大規模な合成とスクリーニングに依存する従来の新薬開発手法と比較して、時間とリソースを大幅に節約できたことを意味します。 化合物30のご紹介 武田薬品の医薬品化学における専門知識を、設計、合成、試験というグローバルなサイクルの中で活用することで、優れた特性を持つ非共有結合型Mpro阻害剤である化合物30の開発に成功しました。 複数のヒトコロナウイルス由来のMproを強力に阻害します。 ヒトプロテアーゼに対して高い選択性を示します。 オミクロン株を含む幅広いウイルス株に対して強力な細胞内抗ウイルス活性を示します。 オミクロン株に対する抗ウイルスアッセイにおいて、ニルマトレルビルよりも約8倍強力です。 初期の研究において、良好な安全性プロファイルと代謝プロファイルを示しています。 今後のステップとして、化合物30の経口バイオアベイラビリティと薬物動態の最適化、臨床開発への移行、およびより広範なコロナウイルス株に対する試験の拡大を進めていきます。 新型コロナウイルスの変異や動物からの感染事例が発生するたびに、ウイルスの進化は絶え間なく続くことを痛感させられます。抗ウイルス薬を開発する理想的なタイミングは、緊急に必要となる前なのです。広範なウイルスに効果を発揮する経口Mpro阻害剤は、新たな変異株に対する耐性を強化し、経口投与可能な低分子医薬品は保管や流通が容易であるため、世界中の人々が治療を受けられる機会を拡大することができます。化合物30は、現在および将来のコロナウイルスによる脅威に対して持続的な防御を提供する次世代抗ウイルス薬開発のための青写真となるものです。この進歩により、次の脅威が現れる前に抗ウイルス薬を準備できる可能性が高まります。 岡部 篤俊 武田薬品工業のコンピュテーショナルサイエンス部門に所属するプリンシパル・サイエンティストです。計算化学者として、30件以上の低分子創薬プロジェクトに携わってきました。東京工業大学にて物理化学を専攻し、学士号および修士号を取得。創薬研究における計算科学の活用を専門とし、分子設計・評価を通じて創薬プロジェクトを支援しています。これまでの研究成果は、Nature Communications、Journal of Medicinal Chemistry、The Journal of Physical Chemistry B などの国際的な学術誌に掲載されています。 また、複数の特許の発明者であり、臨床開発段階に進んだ化合物の創出にも貢献しています。 落田 温子博士 メディシナルケミストリーの専門性とグローバルな協業経験を強みとする、パートナーシップマネジメント担当のアソシエイト・ディレクターです。 北海道大学にて博士号（理学）を取得後、スタンフォード大学で博士研究員として研究に従事。その後、武田薬品工業に入社しました。2017年以降は、Access to Medicine（医薬品アクセス向上）に関する取り組みに貢献するとともに、計算化学と合成化学を融合した COVID-19 関連プログラムを含む、革新的な創薬プロジェクトを主導してきました。 外部プロジェクトの評価や、多国籍・多文化チームのリーダーシップにおいて豊富な実績を有し、戦略的視点と高い科学的厳密性をもって、パートナーシップの推進と治療イノベーションの加速に貢献しています。 アバ・E・レフラー博士 Schrödinger のセラピューティクス部門に所属するシニア・プリンシパル・サイエンティストです。現在は、低分子化合物を中心とした創薬研究に取り組んでいます。プリンストン大学にて化学の学士号を取得（応用数学のサーティフィケート修了）後、D. E. Shaw Research にて研究に従事。その後、ニューヨーク大学医学部（NYU School of Medicine）にて神経科学の博士号を取得しました。これまでの研究成果は、 Science 、 The Journal of Neuroscience 、 ACS Medicinal Chemistry Letters 、 The Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling 、 Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences など、国際的に権威ある学術誌に多数掲載されています。 また、臨床試験段階にある化合物を含む複数の特許の発明者でもあります。 Sign Up Today Sign up to receive quarterly updates with the latest from Extrapolations.
